passages.text: These are additional proverbs of Solomon, which were copied by the men of Hezekiah king of Judah: It is the glory of God to conceal a matter and the glory of kings to search it out.
passages.sermon:
Solomon spoke these proverbs.
The men of Hezekiah, king of Judah, copied them.
God shows His glory by hiding things.
Kings show their glory by searching out matters.
passages.original: גַּם־ אֵ֭לֶּה מִשְׁלֵ֣י שְׁלֹמֹ֑ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר הֶ֝עְתִּ֗יקוּ אַנְשֵׁ֤י׀ חִזְקִיָּ֬ה מֶֽלֶךְ־ יְהוּדָֽה׃ כְּבֹ֣ד אֱ֭לֹהִים הַסְתֵּ֣ר דָּבָ֑ר וּכְבֹ֥ד מְ֝לָכִ֗ים חֲקֹ֣ר דָּבָֽר׃

passages.text: As the heavens are high and the earth is deep, so the hearts of kings cannot be searched.
passages.sermon:
The heavens are very high.
The earth is very deep.
The hearts of kings are impossible to search.
No one can fully understand the thoughts of kings.
passages.original: שָׁמַ֣יִם לָ֭רוּם וָאָ֣רֶץ לָעֹ֑מֶק וְלֵ֥ב מְ֝לָכִ֗ים אֵ֣ין חֵֽקֶר׃

passages.text: Remove the dross from the silver, and a vessel for a silversmith will come forth.
passages.sermon:
Silver often contains dross.
Dross is waste material mixed with the silver.
A silversmith is a person who makes things from silver.
If you remove the dross from the silver, the silver becomes pure.
When the silver is pure, the silversmith can make a useful vessel from it.
passages.original: הָג֣וֹ סִיגִ֣ים מִכָּ֑סֶף וַיֵּצֵ֖א לַצֹּרֵ֣ף כֶּֽלִי׃

passages.text: Remove the wicked from the king’s presence, and his throne will be established in righteousness.
passages.sermon:
A king rules over his people.
A wicked person stands before the king.
Remove the wicked person from the king’s presence.
Then the king’s throne will stand firm in righteousness.
passages.original: הָג֣וֹ רָ֭שָׁע לִפְנֵי־ מֶ֑לֶךְ וְיִכּ֖וֹן בַּצֶּ֣דֶק כִּסְאֽוֹ׃

passages.text: Do not exalt yourself in the presence of the king, and do not stand in the place of great men; for it is better that he says to you, “Come up here!” than that you should be demoted in the presence of the prince. Even what you have seen with your own eyes, do not bring hastily to court. Otherwise, what will you do in the end when your neighbor puts you to shame?
passages.sermon:
Do not make yourself important before the king.
Do not stand in the place where great men stand.
It is better if the king says to you, “Come up here.”
It is better than being brought low before a prince.
This can happen in front of people who have seen you.
Do not quickly bring what you have seen to court.
If you do, your neighbor may shame you in the end.
You will not know what to do when this happens.
passages.original: אַל־ תִּתְהַדַּ֥ר לִפְנֵי־ מֶ֑לֶךְ וּבִמְק֥וֹם גְּ֝דֹלִ֗ים אַֽל־ תַּעֲמֹֽד׃ כִּ֤י ט֥וֹב אֲמָר־ לְךָ֗ עֲ‍ֽלֵ֫ה הֵ֥נָּה מֵֽ֭הַשְׁפִּ֣ילְךָ לִפְנֵ֣י נָדִ֑יב אֲשֶׁ֖ר רָא֣וּ עֵינֶֽיךָ׃ אַל־ תֵּצֵ֥א לָרִ֗ב מַ֫הֵ֥ר פֶּ֣ן מַה־ תַּ֭עֲשֶׂה בְּאַחֲרִיתָ֑הּ בְּהַכְלִ֖ים אֹתְךָ֣ רֵעֶֽךָ׃

passages.text: Argue your case with your neighbor without betraying another’s confidence, lest the one who hears may disgrace you, and your infamy never go away.
passages.sermon:
If you have a dispute, speak directly to your neighbor.
Do not reveal another person's secret.
If you reveal a secret, someone who hears may shame you.
Your bad reputation may never leave you.
passages.original: רִֽ֭יבְךָ רִ֣יב אֶת־ רֵעֶ֑ךָ וְס֖וֹד אַחֵ֣ר אַל־ תְּגָֽל׃ פֶּֽן־ יְחַסֶּדְךָ֥ שֹׁמֵ֑עַ וְ֝דִבָּתְךָ֗ לֹ֣א תָשֽׁוּב׃

passages.text: A word fitly spoken is like apples of gold in settings of silver.
passages.sermon:
A word fitly spoken is valuable.
It is beautiful.
It is like apples made of gold.
These apples sit in settings of silver.
A right word at the right time is precious and lovely.
passages.original: תַּפּוּחֵ֣י זָ֭הָב בְּמַשְׂכִּיּ֥וֹת כָּ֑סֶף דָּ֝בָ֗ר דָּבֻ֥ר עַל־ אָפְנָֽיו׃

passages.text: Like an earring of gold or an ornament of fine gold is a wise man’s rebuke to a listening ear.
passages.sermon:
A wise person gives correction.
A wise person speaks to someone who listens.
This correction is valuable.
This correction is like a gold earring.
This correction is like a fine gold ornament.
A listening person receives the wise correction.
The correction is precious to the listener.
passages.original: נֶ֣זֶם זָ֭הָב וַחֲלִי־ כָ֑תֶם מוֹכִ֥יחַ חָ֝כָ֗ם עַל־ אֹ֥זֶן שֹׁמָֽעַת׃

passages.text: Like the cold of snow in the time of harvest is a trustworthy messenger to those who send him; he refreshes the soul of his masters.
passages.sermon:
A trustworthy messenger brings good news to those who send him.
He is like the cold of snow during harvest time.
He refreshes the soul of his masters.
He gives relief and comfort to those who depend on him.
passages.original: כְּצִנַּת־ שֶׁ֨לֶג׀ בְּי֬וֹם קָצִ֗יר צִ֣יר נֶ֭אֱמָן לְשֹׁלְחָ֑יו וְנֶ֖פֶשׁ אֲדֹנָ֣יו יָשִֽׁיב׃פ

passages.text: Like clouds and wind without rain is the man who boasts of gifts never given.
passages.sermon:
A man boasts about gifts he never gives.
He is like clouds and wind that bring no rain.
Clouds and wind promise rain.
Rain does not come.
A man who promises gifts but does not give them is the same.
He makes promises but does not fulfill them.
passages.original: נְשִׂיאִ֣ים וְ֭רוּחַ וְגֶ֣שֶׁם אָ֑יִן אִ֥ישׁ מִ֝תְהַלֵּ֗ל בְּמַתַּת־ שָֽׁקֶר׃

passages.text: Through patience a ruler can be persuaded, and a gentle tongue can break a bone.
passages.sermon:
A patient person can persuade a ruler.
A gentle tongue can break a bone.
Patience has great power.
Gentle words can overcome strong resistance.
passages.original: בְּאֹ֣רֶךְ אַ֭פַּיִם יְפֻתֶּ֣ה קָצִ֑ין וְלָשׁ֥וֹן רַ֝כָּ֗ה תִּשְׁבָּר־ גָּֽרֶם׃

passages.text: If you find honey, eat just what you need, lest you have too much and vomit it up.
passages.sermon:
If you find honey, eat only what you need.
Do not eat too much honey.
If you eat too much honey, you will become full and vomit.
Honey is sweet, but too much is harmful.
Take only what is enough for you.
passages.original: דְּבַ֣שׁ מָ֭צָאתָ אֱכֹ֣ל דַּיֶּ֑ךָּ פֶּן־ תִּ֝שְׂבָּעֶ֗נּוּ וַהֲקֵֽאתֽוֹ׃

passages.text: Seldom set foot in your neighbor’s house, lest he grow weary and hate you.
passages.sermon:
A neighbor is someone who lives near you.
Do not visit your neighbor’s house often.
If you visit too much, your neighbor may become tired of you.
If your neighbor grows tired of you, he may begin to hate you.
passages.original: הֹקַ֣ר רַ֭גְלְךָ מִבֵּ֣ית רֵעֶ֑ךָ פֶּן־ יִ֝שְׂבָּעֲךָ֗ וּשְׂנֵאֶֽךָ׃

passages.text: Like a club or sword or sharp arrow is a man who bears false witness against his neighbor.
passages.sermon:
A man who gives false testimony against his neighbor is dangerous.
He is like a club.
He is like a sword.
He is like a sharp arrow.
He can cause great harm.
passages.original: מֵפִ֣יץ וְ֭חֶרֶב וְחֵ֣ץ שָׁנ֑וּן אִ֥ישׁ עֹנֶ֥ה בְ֝רֵעֵ֗הוּ עֵ֣ד שָֽׁקֶר׃

passages.text: Like a broken tooth or a foot out of joint is confidence in a faithless man in time of trouble.
passages.sermon:
A faithless man cannot be trusted in times of trouble.
Confidence in a faithless man will fail you when you need help.
This is like a broken tooth that cannot chew.
This is like a foot out of joint that cannot walk.
Both are useless when you need them most.
Trusting a faithless man brings disappointment in difficult times.
passages.original: שֵׁ֣ן רֹ֭עָה וְרֶ֣גֶל מוּעָ֑דֶת מִבְטָ֥ח בּ֝וֹגֵ֗ד בְּי֣וֹם צָרָֽה׃

passages.text: Like one who removes a garment on a cold day or vinegar poured on a wound is one who sings songs to a heavy heart.
passages.sermon:
A person with a heavy heart feels deep sadness.
A person who sings songs to someone with a heavy heart causes pain.
This is like taking off a coat on a cold day.
This is also like pouring vinegar on a wound.
Both actions make the pain worse.
Singing to a sad person does not help them.
It increases their suffering.
passages.original: מַ֥עֲדֶה בֶּ֨גֶד׀ בְּי֣וֹם קָ֭רָה חֹ֣מֶץ עַל־ נָ֑תֶר וְשָׁ֥ר בַּ֝שִּׁרִ֗ים עַ֣ל לֶב־ רָֽע׃פ

passages.text: If your enemy is hungry, give him food to eat, and if he is thirsty, give him water to drink.
passages.sermon:
This passage gives instructions about how to treat your enemy.
If your enemy feels hungry, give him food.
If your enemy feels thirsty, give him water.
Treat your enemy with kindness when he has a need.
passages.original: אִם־ רָעֵ֣ב שֹׂ֭נַאֲךָ הַאֲכִלֵ֣הוּ לָ֑חֶם וְאִם־ צָ֝מֵ֗א הַשְׁקֵ֥הוּ מָֽיִם׃

passages.text: For in so doing, you will heap burning coals on his head, and the LORD will reward you.
passages.sermon:
If you give food to your enemy when he is hungry, you show kindness.
If you give water to your enemy when he is thirsty, you show mercy.
When you do this, you heap burning coals on his head.
The LORD will reward you for your kindness.
passages.original: כִּ֤י גֶֽחָלִ֗ים אַ֭תָּה חֹתֶ֣ה עַל־ רֹאשׁ֑וֹ וַֽ֝יהוָ֗ה יְשַׁלֶּם־ לָֽךְ׃

passages.text: As the north wind brings forth rain, so a backbiting tongue brings angry looks.
passages.sermon:
The north wind brings rain.
A backbiting tongue causes angry looks.
The north wind is strong and cold.
It makes clouds gather and rain fall.
A person who speaks secretly against others stirs up anger.
People show their anger with their faces.
Hidden words can create trouble, just as the wind creates rain.
passages.original: ר֣וּחַ צָ֭פוֹן תְּח֣וֹלֵֽל גָּ֑שֶׁם וּפָנִ֥ים נִ֝זְעָמִ֗ים לְשׁ֣וֹן סָֽתֶר׃

passages.text: Better to live on a corner of the roof than to share a house with a quarrelsome wife.
passages.sermon:
A quarrelsome wife causes strife in the home.
A man may live with her in the same house.
He may find constant conflict there.
It is better for him to live alone on the corner of a roof.
A small, lonely place is better than a large house filled with arguments.
passages.original: ט֗וֹב שֶׁ֥בֶת עַל־ פִּנַּת־ גָּ֑ג מֵאֵ֥שֶׁת מְדוֹנִים וּבֵ֥ית חָֽבֶר׃

passages.text: Like cold water to a weary soul is good news from a distant land.
passages.sermon: Cold water refreshes a tired person.\r\nGood news from far away refreshes a weary soul.\r\nBoth bring relief and strength.
passages.original: מַ֣יִם קָ֭רִים עַל־ נֶ֣פֶשׁ עֲיֵפָ֑ה וּשְׁמוּעָ֥ה ט֝וֹבָ֗ה מֵאֶ֥רֶץ מֶרְחָֽק׃

passages.text: Like a muddied spring or a polluted well is a righteous man who gives way to the wicked.
passages.sermon:
A righteous man is someone who does what is right.
A wicked person does what is evil.
A righteous man should stand firm against the wicked.
If a righteous man gives way to a wicked person, he becomes like a muddied spring.
He also becomes like a polluted well.
A muddied spring cannot give clean water.
A polluted well cannot refresh people.
A righteous man who gives in to evil loses his good influence.
He cannot help others as he should.
passages.original: מַעְיָ֣ן נִ֭רְפָּשׂ וּמָק֣וֹר מָשְׁחָ֑ת צַ֝דִּ֗יק מָ֣ט לִפְנֵֽי־ רָשָֽׁע׃

passages.text: It is not good to eat too much honey or to search out one’s own glory.
passages.sermon:
Honey is sweet.
People enjoy eating honey.
Eating too much honey is not good.
Seeking your own glory is also not good.
Searching for your own honor is like eating too much honey.
Both are harmful.
passages.original: אָ֘כֹ֤ל דְּבַ֣שׁ הַרְבּ֣וֹת לֹא־ ט֑וֹב וְחֵ֖קֶר כְּבֹדָ֣ם כָּבֽוֹד׃

passages.text: Like a city whose walls are broken down is a man who does not control his temper.
passages.sermon:
A man who does not control his temper is like a city with broken walls.
This man cannot restrain his spirit.
This city has no protection.
This man has no self-control.
Enemies can easily enter a city without walls.
Trouble can easily come to a man without self-control.
passages.original: עִ֣יר פְּ֭רוּצָה אֵ֣ין חוֹמָ֑ה אִ֝֗ישׁ אֲשֶׁ֤ר אֵ֖ין מַעְצָ֣ר לְרוּחֽוֹ׃
